column1: # intents.tsv — the intent catalogue. Nothing about intents is compiled in.
#   intent <TAB> id <TAB> priority <TAB> sticky <TAB> hint shown to the orchestrator
#   term   <TAB> id <TAB> phrase that classifies the query ON ITS OWN
#   weak   <TAB> id <TAB> phrase that classifies ONLY alongside another term of
#                         the same intent (>=2 weak, or 1 weak + 1 strong)
#   id        stable identifier. Referenced by term rows AND by the first column
#             of intent-exemplars.tsv — the two files must agree or the exemplar
#             is dropped at startup with a warning.
#   priority  keyword rules are evaluated in ascending priority, first match wins.
#             This is what makes "Nokia handover procedure" route to out_of_scope
#             rather than procedure — it is an ordering decision, not a code path.
#   sticky    true  → when the keyword rule matches, the embedding classifier is
#                     not allowed to override it. Use for signals that are
#             false → the embedding classifier decides; keyword is fallback only.
#   hint      free text appended to the response as "Intent: <hint>".
# The intent with the HIGHEST priority value is the default, used when nothing
# matches. There must be exactly one intent row with no term rows pointing at it
# for that to be meaningful — clause_lookup plays that role here.
# Adding an intent needs no recompile: add an intent row, its term rows, and
# ideally a block of exemplars in intent-exemplars.tsv so the embedding path can

column5: out-of-scope — this looks commercial or time-sensitive (pricing, advisories, roadmaps, outages); not covered by the indexed standards or vendor references, so prefer WebSearch
troubleshooting — cause codes and failure paths; check the protocol spec's cause-value clause as well as the stage-2 flow
procedure — spans stage-2 flow and stage-3 protocol specs; consider getProcedureFlow for a cross-spec evidence bundle
clause-lookup — a single spec normally owns this answer

column1: # ── out_of_scope: vendor / commercial / operational, never in a published spec ─
# Vendor NAMES are `weak` on purpose. A brand name is poor evidence of commercial
# intent: a Bulk-CM payload carries "vendor": "NOKIA" while being a pure
# standards-validation request. Measured — as a strong term, adding "NOKIA" to
# "si-Periodicity allowed values SchedulingInfo" flipped the intent from
# clause-lookup to out-of-scope and told the answer model to distrust perfectly
# good results. As weak terms they need a commercial word beside them.
# 'juniper' removed 2026-07-29: the Junos CLI Reference (28,301 chunks, series
# JUNIPER) is now indexed, so a Junos question is IN scope. Leaving it here made
# search3gpp answer config-audit queries with "prefer WebSearch" while it was
# returning the correct Junos statement in the very same response.
